purpose: A time range for queries over time: logs, events, traces and metrics. After the Console Kit date-time range (quick ranges, absolute range with times, previous and next) and Cloudscape's date range picker. The value is either **relative** (`{ type: 'relative', amount: 15, unit: 'minute' }`, read as "the last 15 minutes" and re-resolved against the clock on every query, so a live view keeps moving) or **absolute** (`{ type: 'absolute', start, end }`, two ISO 8601 instants). The trigger prints `Last 15 minutes` or the absolute range in the selected time zone with its UTC offset. The panel switches between Relative range (the quick ranges and a custom duration) and Absolute range (the `DatePicker` month grid, start and end date and time fields — the times hidden with `showTime` off — and the time zone selector) and commits only on Apply; Cancel and Escape drop the draft. Absolute boundaries are typed as wall-clock time in the selected zone and stored as instants, so the same value reads correctly in every zone. With `showStep`, Previous and Next move the range by its own length. Date math uses `Intl` and the native `Date` only.
useWhen: Use DateRangePicker for any start–end range: relative ('last 24 hours') or absolute, with or without times; turn times off for whole-day reports and billing periods. For one date use DatePicker; to display a moment in time use Timestamp.
Filtering events, logs, traces or metrics by time, where "the last N minutes" must stay relative.
Any range that needs times of day and a time zone, not only dates.
Investigations that page through time window by window (`show-step`).
Whole-day ranges for a report or a billing period: `range-selector-mode="absolute-only"` with `:show-time="false"`.
avoidWhen: A single date or a date and time → use `date-picker`.
A fixed list of named intervals and nothing custom → use `select` or `toggle-group`.
related: `date-picker` — the month grid, the date and time fields and the time zone selector come from its internal parts, so both pickers look and behave the same. Split: DatePicker picks one date (optionally with a time); DateRangePicker owns every range and keeps a relative window relative.
`timestamp` — displays a moment in time; both read the `WebkitProvider` `timeZone`.
`webkit-provider` — its `timeZone` is the zone the picker formats in while `v-model:time-zone` is unbound.
`field` — inside a `Field`, the trigger takes the field's label (`for` points at it), description, `invalid` and `disabled`.
`property-filter` — the query bar it sits next to in an events toolbar.
`chart` — the histogram whose brush usually writes an absolute range back into this picker.
bestPractices: Keep relative values relative: resolve them to instants when the query runs (`now - amount × unit` to `now`), never when the user picks them. `useTimeRange(value)` from `@aziontech/webkit/use-time-range` returns `from` and `to` and holds the window until `refresh()`; its `TIME_RANGE_PRESETS` (last hour, 24 hours, 7 days, 30 days) go in `relative-options`.

Fix the reference clock in tests, demos and server-rendered pages so labels and step limits are deterministic: `now` on the app's `WebkitProvider` covers every picker below it; the `now` prop overrides it for one picker.
Bind `v-model:time-zone` to the user's saved preference, and show times elsewhere on the page in the same zone.
Set `max` (usually now) and `min` (the retention limit) instead of validating after Apply.
Name the picker after what it filters (`aria-label="Events time range"`).
